about: Lessons for Learn (F1). Each step has text, optionally a task to switch to first ({"task": "library"}; tasks.js), a control to point at ({"setting": name} or {"element": id}) and a goal that moves on by itself when met: {"changed": name}, {"setting": name, "above": n} or {"below": n}, {"history": label}. Without a goal, Next moves on. Translations can be added as more files later.

lessons.title: Getting around
lessons.summary: Tasks, the library, search and where everything is, in two minutes. No photo needed.

steps.text: Ambrotype is split into tasks, along the top: Library to find and sort photos, Develop to edit one, and Color, Retouch, Film and Collage, which show only what that job needs. Ctrl+Alt+1 to 6 switch between them.

This is the Library. The Folders panel lists your library folders: add one with +, and every photo in it (and its subfolders) is in the catalogue. Photos on a drive that isn't plugged in stay listed, greyed out.
Filter narrows the grid by rating, flag, colour label, keyword or camera; Import copies photos in from a card. 1–5 rate, P and X pick and reject, 6–9 add a colour label.
‹ and › fold the sides away for a bigger grid (Ctrl+[ and Ctrl+]). Double-click a photo to edit it.
Develop is the full editor: the panels on the right are Lightroom's, with its sliders and ranges. Each task remembers the layout you pick while in it.
Lost a control? Press Ctrl+K (⌘K on a Mac) and type a few letters: it finds any command, setting, panel, preset, layout or theme, even one this layout doesn't show.

Every command is also in the menu bar, with its keys: at the top of the screen on a Mac; on Windows and Linux, turn it on in Settings → General. Settings also has every shortcut on a keyboard map, to change any.
Appearance changes the layout and the colours; Edit layout moves panels and buttons by dragging. Browse gets layouts, themes, presets, plugins and even whole other interfaces that people shared.
Something wrong, or an idea? Feedback opens a report with the details filled in. F1 brings these lessons back any time.

lessons.title: Editing basics
lessons.summary: White balance, light, contrast and colour on the photo you have open, in about five minutes.

steps.text: Every change you make is a setting, saved next to the photo in an .xmp file that Lightroom reads too. Nothing changes the photo itself. Let's start at the top of Basic.
White balance makes white look white. Move Temp: left is cooler (bluer), right is warmer. Try a little, then settle where the greys look neutral.
Exposure sets the overall brightness, in stops. Make the photo as bright as it should be in the middle tones; don't worry about the sky yet.
Highlights brings back detail in the bright parts (a sky, a white shirt). Pull it to the left, below −10.
Shadows opens up the dark parts without making the blacks grey. Push it to the right, above +10.
Whites and Blacks set where the brightest and darkest tones end. Press J for the clipping overlay (red: blown highlights, blue: crushed shadows), then move Blacks a little.
Vibrance strengthens the quieter colours and leaves skin and strong colours mostly alone; Saturation moves all colours alike. Give the photo some Vibrance.
Press \ (backslash), or Before / After, to compare with the photo as it came from the camera. Press it again to come back.
Every step is in History. Click an earlier line to go back to it; your later steps stay there (greyed) until you make a new change.
Not sure where to start on the next photo? Auto, beside Tone, sets the six tone sliders for you; then adjust from there. That's the basics. Ctrl+S saves the edit to the sidecar.

lessons.title: Coming from Lightroom
lessons.summary: Where Lightroom's panels, presets and shortcuts are here.

steps.text: Ambrotype reads and writes Lightroom's own settings: a raw's .xmp sidecar opens here as Lightroom left it, and our edits open in Lightroom. Add your photo folders in the Library task (G); nothing is copied or converted.
Lightroom's presets work as they are. Lightroom's own preset folder is found by itself; Add folder… adds others (.xmp and .lrtemplate). Amount scales a preset, as in Lightroom.
The panels on the right are the Develop module's, with Lightroom's sliders and ranges. Edit layout (in Appearance) moves them, and Appearance changes how they look.

Masks (M), Spot removal (Q), Crop (R) and the white balance picker (W) are on the toolbar. Many of Lightroom's shortcuts work here, and Settings (the ⚙ button) shows all of them on a keyboard map, where you can change any.
Edits save to the sidecar with Ctrl+S, and when you move to another photo. Lightroom picks them up with Metadata → Read Metadata from File.
